title: Wiring a Portable Generator to a Home: Transfer Switch, Interlock, and Safety
summary: This video demonstrates practical approaches to powering a home with a portable generator. It covers essential safety guidance for outdoor operation to avoid carbon monoxide poisoning, methods to feed a home from a generator using a power inlet box and backfed wiring, and two main approaches for safe electrical integration: a transfer switch that selects critical circuits and an interlock that isolates the generator from street power. The host emphasizes prioritizing critical loads (furnace, refrigerator, heating) and performing a controlled restoration by turning on loads one by one to avoid overloading the generator. It also cautions against running high-draw appliances (oven, dryer, central air) during a outage and notes that a generator has limited capacity relative to a whole-house load.
topics: generator CO sensor and automatic shut-off
backfeed wiring to a home panel
load restoration sequence (one circuit at a time)
avoidance of heavy loads (oven, dryer, central AC)

sections.title: Safety: CO hazards and outdoor use
sections.description: The hosts warn about carbon monoxide from portable generators and insist they be operated outside. One unit reputedly includes a built-in CO sensor that can shut the generator off if CO is detected.

sections.title: CO safety and external power connections
sections.description: Extension cords are commonly used but not ideal for powering a home. The discussion introduces feeding the home through a power inlet box rather than running power directly into living spaces.

sections.title: Wiring from power inlet to back of the house and main panel
sections.description: A cord from the generator is connected to a power inlet box, which then feeds wiring back to the home and ties into the main panel.

sections.title: Transfer switch approach for selective circuits
sections.description: The transfer switch option is introduced: a 10-circuit unit is used to select the most critical circuits to power when the grid is down.

sections.title: Interlock method: generator inlet and safety isolation
sections.description: An interlock approach is described as an alternative to a transfer switch, where the outside inlet connects to a breaker and the interlock prevents backfeeding when the main is on.

sections.title: Startup sequence and safe switching with interlock
sections.description: Demonstrates the sequence: turn the main power off, use the interlock, start the generator, and perform controlled switching to energize circuits.

sections.title: Load management during restoration
sections.description: Guidance on restoring critical services by bringing loads back online one at a time to avoid overloading the generator.

sections.title: Cautions and closing guidance
sections.description: Reaffirms safety cautions about large appliances and closes with general channel guidance and a call to action.
